description:
Functional specifications covered with associated files to edit/add:
New package PairingSession reuses ConnectionWorker/Adapter. Move generic begin/status/retry/cancel, provisional profile allocation, parent monitoring, configurable TTL, identity readiness/refresh, displayed-identity confirmation guard, stale-event rejection and transport cleanup from ZAQ session.ex. Generic caller ownership must be explicit and checked for every command. Host controls access through existing Action; no BOActor, NodeRouter, Ecto or connector schema in package. Public status excludes raw snapshots; provisional messages remain discarded.

Tests to add before implementation:
Before code: standalone non-ZAQ host lifecycle tests; QR expiry/retry; unknown/changed identity; wrong owner; parent death; TTL; temporary-store/transport failure; cancellation/logout failure cleanup; no provisional chat ingress; stale events and concurrent commands.

Branches/paths validated:
Pairing, connected, expired, disconnected; owner gone; identity unavailable/changed; premature confirm; retry/cancel.

Mocking plan:
Real internal collaborators; inject external transport/host-callback edges only. Isolated BEAMs for global Mnesia. Explicit config/clock/dependency options.

Documentations to update for both code and docs/ related content:
Package PairingSession API and lifecycle contract, README examples; preserve existing UI response behavior.

Action reuse assessment:
Extend existing ConnectionWorker/Adapter lifecycle rather than create parallel transport. Generic session machinery is package-local; host PairLinkedDevice Action remains authorization entry point.

Validation and E2E:
Read owning AGENTS.md and ZAQ workflow, action-reuse, testing, system-config and documentation policies as applicable. Use real internal state/process/DB boundaries; mock only external WhatsApp transport or package host-callback boundary in upstream standalone tests. Isolate global Mnesia tests in separate BEAMs. Runtime dependency seams use explicit public options. Preserve current UI journeys; run relevant existing tests, no new feature E2E authoring unless scope changes and the required UX approval is recorded. Follow post-review coverage and final validation gates; no automatic commit/push/publication.
